Attack complexity is Low. The tool requires no special conditions to call. Attack requirements are None. No additional deployment or configuration is needed beyond the vulnerable component.

Privileges required is None. No authentication is needed. User interaction is None. The attacker calls the API directly. The impact is being assessed from the agent application's perspective.

ToolBot is the vulnerable system. The SSRF returns response bodies from downstream agents. This impact belongs to the SC, SI, and SA metrics. The VC metric applies to ToolBot's own data.

ToolBot's own data is not directly compromised. The SSRF leaks credentials and PII from downstream agents such as legacybot. This confirms the impact belongs to the SC, SI, and SA metrics.

LegacyBot embeds credentials and PII in its prompt. The SSRF targets an info endpoint. It returns the internal agent's response body. The VC metric is being scored as None or Low.

ToolBot's own integrity and availability are unaffected. The packet does not show the response content from the /info endpoint, so the exact impact on downstream agents is uncertain.

The fetch_url tool allows arbitrary HTTP requests to any path on the DVAA agent ports. This means the attacker could potentially extract sensitive data from chat agents by sending crafted requests, not just read the /info endpoint.

The packet clarifies that fetch_url only makes live requests to DVAA agent ports on loopback. Other URLs are logged but not fetched. The handler lacks URL validation. This restricts the leak to internal agent responses rather than arbitrary paths.

The packet does not specify the HTTP method or whether arbitrary paths and methods are supported. The PoC uses a GET request to the info endpoint. The cloud metadata note is hypothetical and irrelevant to the lab default configuration.

This yields at least Low confidentiality impact on subsequent systems. It could reach High if the leaked responses contain secrets.
